issues.legal_issue: A State Government may reserve mineral-bearing land owned by the State for exploitation in the public sector and refuse private applications for mineral concessions over that land.
material_facts: The State Government owned the minerals and mines in the areas concerned.
The State Government notified that the areas were reserved for exploitation of bauxite in the public sector.
Private applicants sought mining leases over the reserved areas, and the State Government refused their applications on that ground.
issues.conclusion: The State Government had authority to reserve the areas and refuse the applications while the areas remained reserved.
issues.legal_principle: The Mines and Minerals (Regulation and Development) Act, 1957 declared under section 2 that regulation of mines and mineral development was to be under Union control to the extent provided by the Act, displacing the State Legislature’s power under Entry 23 of List II in that field. That did not divest the State of ownership of minerals within its territory. Sections 4 and 10 and the Rules govern private prospecting and mining concessions; section 10’s power to entertain applications includes power to refuse a concession because the land is unavailable after reservation. Section 17(2) and (4) do not exhaust the State’s authority to reserve land for itself. Rule 59 contemplates State reservation for any purpose. The Court distinguished State of Orissa v. Union of India, AIR 1972 Orissa 68, and found that M/s S. Lal and Co. Ltd. v. Union of India, AIR 1975 Patna 44, did not assist the applicants.

predicates.mineral_concession_refusal_appeal: A party appealed from the refusal of an application for a prospecting licence or mining lease over mineral-bearing land.
predicates.state_owns_minerals: The State Government owned the minerals and mines in the area concerned.
predicates.state_reserved_area_for_public_exploitat: The State Government reserved the area for exploitation in the public sector.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns refusal of a mineral concession, the State owns the minerals, and the State has reserved the area for public-sector exploitation, the State may reserve the land and refuse private concessions while it remains reserved.

issues.legal_issue: An application for a mineral concession over reserved land may be rejected as premature when the land has not again become available for grant and that availability has not been notified.
material_facts: The State Government had reserved the areas for public-sector exploitation.
The applicants applied for mining leases while the areas remained reserved.
The State Government had not made the areas available again for mineral concessions or notified their availability.
The State Government rejected the applications as premature, and the Central Government dismissed the applicants’ revision applications.
issues.conclusion: The State Government was entitled to reject the applications as premature, and the Central Government was justified in dismissing the revision applications.
issues.legal_principle: Rules 58, 59 and 60 of the Mineral Concession Rules, 1960 operate together: a person may not apply for a concession over reserved land until it again becomes available and the State Government notifies that availability; an application made before then is premature and is not to be entertained. Section 13 of the Act authorizes the rules. The Court also relied on the State’s ownership of the minerals and its authority to reserve land.

predicates.reserved_area_concession_application_app: A party appealed after the State Government refused an application for a mineral concession over reserved land and the reviewing authority dismissed a challenge to that refusal.
predicates.application_made_during_reservation: The applicant applied for a mineral concession while the area remained reserved.
predicates.area_not_again_made_available_and_notifi: The State Government had neither made the reserved area available again for mineral concessions nor notified its availability.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns an application made during reservation, and the area has not again been made available and notified, the application may be rejected as premature and the dismissal of the challenge may be upheld.
